name: May 2024 Gannon Geomagnetic Storm
explanation: The Sun sent several big bursts of charged particles toward Earth. They made the sky glow with colorful auroras far from the poles.
funFact: Did you know? People saw auroras as far south as Florida during this storm.

name: October 2003 Halloween Solar Storms
explanation: The Sun unleashed an enormous flare and a fast cloud of particles. The storm disturbed radio signals and made bright auroras appear in unusual places.
funFact: Did you know? One flare was so powerful that scientists had to estimate its strength because their measuring instrument was overwhelmed.

name: St. Patrick's Day Geomagnetic Storm
explanation: A cloud of material from the Sun reached Earth and stirred up our planet's magnetic surroundings. It sparked bright auroras and caused some radio and navigation hiccups.
funFact: Did you know? This was the strongest geomagnetic storm in more than a decade at the time.

name: September 2017 Solar Storm
explanation: The Sun fired off a powerful flare and sent a burst of particles into space. The activity caused short-lived radio trouble and helped paint the sky with auroras.
funFact: Did you know? The flare came from a sunspot region that produced several strong flares in just a few days.

name: March 2012 Solar Storm
explanation: Two powerful solar flares erupted close together, sending fast-moving particles away from the Sun. Earth felt a strong space-weather disturbance when some of that material arrived.
funFact: Did you know? The flares came from one busy sunspot region that kept producing space weather for days.

name: March 2023 Geomagnetic Storm
explanation: A fast-moving cloud from the Sun reached Earth and stirred up its magnetic field. The storm made auroras visible much farther from the poles than usual.
funFact: Did you know? Some people in the southern United States spotted auroras during this storm.
